About

A beginner-friendly online boot2root CTF. Each team gets a vulnerable virtual machine (OVA) to run locally. Your job is to find your way in, escalate privileges to root, and capture the flags along the way. 

Format and Schedule

  • Mode: Online (the VM runs on your own machine)
  • Date: 29 October 2026
  • Start: 6:00 PM IST

Eligibility

  • Open to all college students
  • Inter-college teams: allowed
  • Team size: up to 3 members 
  • Each person can be on only one team

How it works

  • Register on Unstop.
  • The encrypted OVA download link will be shared on 29th so you can download it before the event. The password will be released at 6:00 PM on 29 October.
  • Import the OVA into VirtualBox or VMware, find the target IP, and start hacking.
  • Submit flags on the CTF platform(The URL will also be given on the day of the event). The scoreboard updates live.

System requirements

  • VirtualBox or VMware (latest version)
  • An attacker machine of your choice (Kali Linux, Parrot, or your own setup)

Rules

  • Internet access and public tools are allowed.
  • Do not share flags, hints, or solutions with other teams during the event. Collusion leads to disqualification.
  • Attack only your own local VM. Do not attack the CTF platform, other participants, or any other infrastructure.
  • Do not attempt to brute-force or spam the flag submission page.
  • Do not publish writeups or walkthroughs until the organizers announce the event is over.
  • Flag format: [flag format, e.g. CTF{...}]
  • Ranking: by number of points, ties broken by who reached the score first.
  • Organizers’ decisions are final. Any rule violation can lead to disqualification.
  • If your VM breaks, re-import the original OVA. Contact the organizers if something is wrong with the machine itself.
  • winners must submit a brief write-up explaining their CTF solution. Prizes will be awarded only after verifying that no malpractice occured. 

Prize Pool INR 20k
